transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... it's just gotten to be too much. My in-laws, they aren't just arguing with me anymore. I know what they're doing. They're using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They're trying to make everyone forget everything I've done for this family, and it's just... it's very clear to me now what's happening.
Can you tell me more about what makes you think your in-laws are trying to push you out?

Well, like I was saying, it's just obvious to me. It goes way beyond normal family bickering. I know for a fact they are using the altar and the parish committee against me. 

They want to push me out of the picture completely. It's all about making sure everyone at the church and in the community forgets all the hard work and everything I've done for this family over the years. I just... I know exactly what they're doing, and it's very real.
Can you explain how you know for sure that your in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee against you? Have you noticed any specific actions or evidence that makes you certain of this?

Well, it's... you just see it in how they act. It's not like they handed me a letter announcing it. I see them whispering with the committee members right up by the altar after mass. They make sure I'm not included in any of the church planning anymore. 

It's their way of... of erasing me. They're setting it up so the whole parish forgets all the years I spent helping this family and volunteering. I don't need a piece of paper to prove it, I just see it happening right in front of me. They are absolutely using the church to push me out, plain and simple.
Do you feel certain that your in-laws are intentionally trying to erase you, even though they haven’t directly said or done anything that most people would see as proof?

Yes, I am absolutely certain. Like I said when I first came in, I know they aren't just arguing with me anymore. They are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They want to make everyone forget everything I have done for this family. I don't need what other people call proof... I just know it.
Even though there’s no clear proof, like a letter or direct statement, do you still feel completely certain that your in-laws are using the church against you?

Yes, I am completely certain. I know I've said it a few times now, but that's exactly why I came in here today. It's not just regular arguing with my in-laws anymore. I know for a fact they are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They are doing it on purpose so that everyone forgets everything I've done for this family. I don't need a letter to know what's going on right in front of my face.

Have you ever had other strong beliefs or knowings like this that others might not share or understand, such as feeling like you have special powers, a special mission, or that you're receiving messages from others that no one else can hear?

I don't know about special powers or missions... but I guess I have experienced some things my husband couldn't understand. 

On several nights recently, I've heard my late mother's voice. She was telling me exactly where to put the marigolds and the candles. It was very clear to me. And then once, I actually saw her standing right near the kitchen doorway. My husband was there and he said no one was there, but... well, I know I saw her.
How often have you heard your late mother's voice or seen her, and have these experiences happened at times when you knew you weren't dreaming or sleepy?

Well, I'd say I heard her voice maybe three or four times, and I saw her just that one time. And I was definitely awake, not dreaming. But... it really only happened during that stretch when I was barely sleeping at all, just rushing around constantly. I felt so sure I had this... this special duty to fix the altar and make it right. 

Later on, when my mood completely dropped and I just felt so heavy and guilty and sad... I wasn't hearing or seeing her anymore. It stopped when I crashed.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you were absolutely sure something was true, even if others couldn't see or prove it, and it turned out later to be incorrect or not based in reality?

No, I don't think so. Aside from what I just told you about my mother, and what my in-laws are doing with the church... no, I haven't had any other experiences like that. I mean, I'm sure about what's happening now, but I haven't had anything else in the past where I believed something that turned out to be wrong.
Have there been times when you were absolutely sure something was true, but it had nothing to do with your in-laws or your mother, and others couldn’t see it or agree with you?

No, honestly, it really is just the situation with my husband's family. That's the whole reason I came in, actually. I just know my in-laws aren't just having a normal argument with me. They are actively using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They're trying to make everyone forget what I have done for this family. 

So... no, apart from what they are doing, and what I experienced with my mother, there isn't anything else.
Have you ever believed that you understood things or saw the truth about situations in a way that most people couldn't, even when they disagreed with you or thought you were wrong?

Well, during that time when I wasn't sleeping and felt so energized... yes. I truly believed I was the only one who could save our family's traditions. I just knew that if people would just listen to me and do exactly what I said, the whole community event would be absolutely perfect. I felt like I saw the whole picture, how everything needed to be, and nobody else seemed to understand how important it was or how to do it right.
Have you ever had a period of time, lasting at least a few days, where your mood was unusually high, overly irritable, or you felt like you didn’t need as much sleep?

Yes, definitely. Like I mentioned a minute ago about that time I had all that energy... there were days when I felt just so bright and certain about everything. But at the same time, I was very quick to anger. If anyone questioned me about the altar, I would just snap at them. It felt like they were insulting my whole family, and I just wouldn't tolerate it.
How long did you feel that way, with your mood being unusually high or irritable and feeling like you didn’t need much sleep?

Well, let me think. This whole crisis has been going on for about two months now. It really all started right after the big fight I had with my in-laws over the Día de los Muertos altar. That's when all of this energy and the irritability really began, and it's just been going ever since.
During that time when you felt so energized and irritable, did you actually sleep less than usual, like only a few hours a night, and still feel fully rested?

Yes, at first that's exactly what happened. I was sleeping only a couple of hours a night, but I'd still get right up to make my lists. I had plenty of energy. But... well, it's not like that now. Lately, I just lie awake way before dawn, just worrying about things, and I never feel rested at all.
During the time when you felt so energized and irritable, did you also find yourself talking more than usual, thinking very fast, being easily distracted, or taking on many tasks at once?

Yes, I did. My daughter actually told me that I was talking so fast about my plans and all our family history that she couldn't even get a word in. To me, it just felt like... well, I felt like I had to keep explaining everything right then and there, before the ideas just disappeared from my head.

During that time when you felt so energized and irritable, was there a period where you felt your mood was abnormally high or elated, not just overly confident or certain, and did that last for at least a week?

Yes, it was definitely like that for at least a week, maybe more. There were days when I felt... well, just so bright and certain about everything I was doing. But it would turn quickly. If anyone questioned me about the altar, I would just snap right at them. I'd get so angry, like they were insulting my whole family.
